articles.headline: Wesley Fofana booed by Chelsea fans against Nottingham Forest over interview comments
articles.description: Chelsea fans booed Wesley Fofana during the early stages of the visit to Nottingham Forest after his controversial unauthorised interview.
articles.body:
Chelsea fans booed Wesley Fofana during the early stages of the visit to Nottingham Forest after his controversial unauthorised interview and endured a harrowing night on the pitch at the City Ground.

The centre-back gave away a penalty for a rash foul that was converted by Morgan Gibbs-White and was susbequently substituted by Xabi Alonso before the hour-mark in the game.

The Blues defender drew criticism earlier in the week for talking for almost two hours with French YouTuber Zack Nani on a range of topics, admitting that he came close to quitting football whilst he was sidelined with an anterior cruciate injury, while also appearing to joke about missing his penalty during last month's Carabao Cup shootout defeat to Liverpool.

Fofana apologised for the interview and boss Xabi Alonso said the matter was closed, but visiting supporters were less forgiving.

They jeered their own player when he was in possession.

- Raheem Sterling avoids jail for dangerous driving

- Tom Brady tops list of athletes who became owners

It has been a particularly difficult spell for Fofana, who has been singled out for poor performances during the team's bad run. His poor form carried into the City Ground, where his error and subsequent foul on Liam Delap saw him concede a penalty early in the second-half.

Chelsea had endured a tough start at the City Ground as they fell behind to Igor Jesus' brilliant fifth-minute strike. Gibbs-White's penalty doubled the hosts' lead soon after the break. 

Fofana's foul on Delap earned him a booking and led to Alonso taking him off in the 56th minute in favour of Levi Colwill. 

Information from PA contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Ravens' Marlon Humphrey to return to lineup; role uncertain
articles.description: Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey will play Sunday against the Texans, a week after he was benched for making disparaging comments about the city of Baltimore.
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey will play Sunday at the Houston Texans, which comes a week after he was benched for making a derogatory comment about the city of Baltimore on his podcast.

It's unknown whether Humphrey will keep his starting job. Humphrey, who is Baltimore's fourth-highest paid defensive player, worked with special teams at the start of Friday's practice.

Ravens coach Jesse Minter acknowledged Humphrey would play after being noncommittal about his status earlier this week

"I think he's handled [the week back] well and like a pro," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said after Friday's practice. "So, he's back in here. He's done a good job and he's ready to try to help the team."

Last week, the Ravens sent Humphrey home after he took a swipe at Baltimore on his podcast "The Marlon Humphrey Show." Asked what Baltimore was best at making, Humphrey quipped, "They're best at making criminals."

Humphrey later apologized for his comments, and the Ravens disciplined him by making him inactive for Sunday's 35-33 loss at the Carolina Panthers. He returned to the team facility on Monday and practiced all week.

It's possible that Humphrey will back up T.J. Tampa, who made an interception in the end zone last week. On Monday, Minter said Tampa "certainly has earned the right to be on the field."

In injury news, Baltimore ruled out right guard Olaivavega Ioane and defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike for Sunday's game.

Ioane, the No. 14 overall pick in this year's draft, hurt his hand in practice on Thursday and didn't practice Friday. This is the second missed game of the season for Ioane, who did not play in Week 8 because of a knee injury.

The Ravens, who have started three different right guards, will likely replace Ioane with Chuma Edoga or Emery Jones Jr.

"I don't think it'll be really long-term, but we'll see," Minter said of Ioane. "Fortunately, we do have the bye next week, so we'll see how the timeline ends up."

Madubuike will miss his second straight game with a hamstring injury. Broderick Washington is expected to fill in for Madubuike, a two-time Pro Bowl lineman.

The Ravens (4-7) have the NFL's longest active losing streak at six games.

articles.headline: Saints rule TE Juwan Johnson out vs. Bengals; TE Noah Fant questionable
articles.description: The Saints ruled out tight end Juwan Johnson with a hamstring and wrist injuries while backup Noah Fant is questionable with a calf injury vs. the Bengals.
articles.body:
METAIRIE, La. -- The New Orleans Saints will be short-handed at tight end for Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Juwan Johnson has been ruled out after missing the week of practice due to a hamstring injury he suffered last Sunday against the Chicago Bears. He was also listed as having a wrist injury.

Johnson was a key part of the Saints offense at the beginning of the season and had three touchdowns in the first three weeks but has had only four catches for 62 yards and a touchdown in the past three games.

 

Noah Fant, who signed with the Saints this season after spending 2025 in Cincinnati, is questionable with a calf injury. Saints coach Kellen Moore said the injury was reported on Friday but is something that has been lingering for a while.

Rookie third-pick Oscar Delp will be in line for a bigger role if both players are out.

"Obviously he plays an important role on special teams. I think that's important when you're kind of that third tight end," Moore said. " ... When he's hopped in there, I thought he's made some productive plays. ... Certainly, you can anticipate probably some more opportunities for him, which will be important. I think he'll do great.

The Saints will get back starting center Erik McCoy (bicep) after he missed the past two games as well as linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring), while right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee) is questionable.

articles.headline: Cardinals to start QB Josh Johnson again with Carson Beck (back spasms) out
articles.description: Cardinals rookie QB Carson Beck will miss a second straight game as he recovers from back spasms, paving the way for veteran Josh Johnson to start vs. the Commanders.
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck will miss a second straight game on Sunday as he continues to deal with back spasms, coach Mike LaFleur said Friday.

Veteran Josh Johnson will get his second straight start Sunday against the Washington Commanders, one of his 14 former NFL teams.

After claiming Kedon Slovis, who spent last season and training camp with the Cardinals, off waivers this week, how Arizona's quarterback depth chart will play out will be disclosed Sunday. LaFleur said he'll keep the details of who'll back up Johnson "in-house right now."

LaFleur said next week "is in play" for Beck. LaFleur added that Beck is frustrated with not being able to get on the field the past two weeks.

"He wants to be out there in the worst way, obviously, but ... not even just a quarterback. You got back spasms. I don't care who you are, and I get there's different degrees of it, but he's trending well and we'll see kind of what it looks like, and I wouldn't even say on Monday, even today he's going to go work out, he's going to work out Saturday, Sunday, all that," LaFleur said. "I don't know the exact plan in terms of he's going to throw every single day, but we'll know more early in the week.

"But, I think frustrated is probably the right word."

Johnson threw for 155 yards and a touchdown on 18-of-31 passing Sunday in a 34-7 loss to the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium.

Being able to practice for a full week has given Johnson the chance to get more comfortable with the offense and the players around him.

"It's been, obviously, just a different type of calm to the situation," Johnson said. "Being able to get some reps and then get the kinks out and kind of see what guys are going to do [in] real time versus that being their first rep on the Sunday.

"Just the little stuff, like my mind slowing down, really kind of playing above the neck like I like to do, not just up there like what is the play again? Actually this is the play, this is where guy's going to be. And actually processing the defense and the cadences and all those different things. Kind of just playing quarterback. I'm looking forward to that part of this week."

Beck has been improving the way the Cardinals were "anticipating based off our prior experiences with him," LaFleur said. LaFleur explained that after the spasms returned late in practice on Nov. 19, they're "bad initially and then it's going to get a little bit better by the day."

"I know he's feeling better, which is, again, all you can hope for in these situations is improvement," LaFleur said, "and so he's feeling better."

articles.headline: Lakers' Austin Reaves available vs. Spurs after missing 5 games with heel bruise
articles.description: Lakers guard Austin Reaves is available to play in Friday night's NBA Cup matchup against the Spurs after missing the past five games with a heel bruise.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Lakers guard Austin Reaves is available to play Friday against the San Antonio Spurs after more than a two-week absence because of a left heel bruise, the team announced.

Reaves suffered the injury on Nov. 11 against the Milwaukee Bucks and went through his first full practice on his road to recovery Wednesday. Reaves told reporters he tried out "a million" different insoles to find the best support for his left foot.

The sixth-year guard was averaging 24.7 points on 51.3% shooting from the floor and 40.9% from 3 with 4.7 assists before the injury.

L.A. went 4-1 without Reaves to stay atop the Western Conference standings. The Lakers (15-3) have a half-game lead over the Spurs (15-4) for No. 1 in the West heading into Friday's game, which is the last day of the NBA Cup qualifying round.

The Lakers, Spurs, Golden State Warriors and Portland Trail Blazers all have a 2-1 record in the West's Group C. L.A. will clinch the group and advance to the quarterfinals of the NBA Cup with a win over San Antonio and a Golden State loss to the Blazers on Friday.

articles.headline: Is Arsenal-Man City still the biggest PL match of the season?
articles.description: Arsenal vs. Man City was supposed to be the Premier League's marquee fixture, but it feels anything but in light of City's guilty verdict. What does Sunday's game really mean?
articles.body:
Two Premier League title contenders face each other Sunday, with one of the sides simultaneously favorites to be relegated. This is the bizarre state of flux that English football's top division now finds itself in.

Arsenal versus Manchester City is the biggest game of the 2026-27 season to date, but chances are it will have only a negligible bearing on the outcome of the title race. Three points, as always, is the prize, yet many people -- including the bookmakers -- expect City to receive a sporting punishment that dwarfs that figure after being found guilty on 114 counts of breaking Premier League financial rules over a nine-year period up to 2018.

Sanctions ranged from expulsion to a huge points deduction and a record fine. City continue to strongly protest their innocence, and an appeal over the guilty verdicts is expected to be heard next month. In the meantime, we are all asked to pretend this is just another normal season with usual rhythm, the usual ebb and flow.

Managers Mikel Arteta and Enzo Maresca certainly sought to give that impression in their prematch news conferences Friday.

"I think when we have two teams at the level that they are both at right now, with the quality players they have on that pitch, it is a massive game and a big game to enjoy I think," said Arteta, noting "that's the only thing we that should put the energy and focus in, there is nothing else."

Said Maresca: "Sunday is important, 100%, but for us it is a long season. We will see February and March where we are and from there you can set up the goals. Now I think it's useless to speak about targets or where we can be at the end of the season."

- Maresca backs Man City to get a win at Arsenal

- Dortmund draw shows that the jury is still out on Gyökeres

But what is the mood behind the scenes in both camps really like? And what does this game really mean?

Arsenal need a statement win

There is little love lost between these two sides, and a genuine rivalry has formed on the pitch as Arsenal cemented their status as City's principal challengers in recent years before finally snatching the crown last season. Watch Erling Haaland and Gabriel Magalhães go at it once again this weekend as they always do.

Sources have also suggested City have grown skeptical of Arsenal off the field over the years, perhaps dating back to the Gunners snatching Arteta from Pep Guardiola's coaching staff in December 2019. Recent tensions between City and many other Premier League clubs over the whole charges saga have done little to quell such ill feelings.

Arsenal are, in theory, the team that stands to benefit most from City's potential demise. articles.headline: NFL Week 12 uniforms: Rams debut alternates, Cowboys rock Thanksgiving throwbacks
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 12, led by an alternate uniform for the Los Angeles Rams.
articles.body:
The NFL on Thanksgiving is a classic tradition, and the uniforms are as much a part of the games as a celebratory turkey leg. But, this year a game was played on Thanksgiving Eve for the first time. And it's only right that the matchup included the debut of a uniform, too. 

The Los Angeles Rams wore their "Fearsome White" threads against the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday. The all-white look is inspired by the Rams' "Fearsome Foursome" defensive line from the 1960s and early 1970s. A modern "Rams Royal" lid includes white horns, white facemask, new 3D bumper logos and "Rams" on the front. Royal blue stripes run over the shoulder to mirror the curve of the helmet horn, alongside accenting sleeve numbers.

The fifth annual John Madden celebration was held on Thanksgiving, and a patch featuring a silhouette of Madden was included on the jersey of each player at all of the Wednesday and Thursday games.

A Thanksgiving tripleheader meant throwback threads, led by the Dallas Cowboys who rocked their 1960s-era uniforms against the Philadelphia Eagles. Dallas brought this combination back in 2022 following a nine-year hiatus. The navy and white look includes a clean lid with a navy star on the side and a stripe down the middle. 

On Black Friday, the Pittsburgh Steelers dressed for the occasion with their color rush threads against the Denver Broncos. The all-black look includes gold numbers and stripes on the sleeves, with a similarly colored stripe down the pants. Pittsburgh owns a 9-3 record in the uniform.

The holiday slate isn't the only place to find uniform heat. The Los Angeles Chargers are wearing their "Super Chargers" all-navy ensemble against the New England Patriots. It's color rush week for the New Orleans Saints with an all-white combination versus the Cincinnati Bengals. The Cleveland Browns are rocking their all-brown "Alpha Dawg" look against the Las Vegas Raiders on "Sunday Night Football."

articles.headline: Timberwolves downgrade star LaMelo Ball to out with ankle sprain
articles.description: The Minnesota Timberwolves downgraded star guard LaMelo Ball to out for Friday night's NBA Cup game vs. the Memphis Grizzlies due to a left ankle sprain.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Timberwolves downgraded star guard LaMelo Ball to out for Friday night's NBA Cup game vs. the Memphis Grizzlies due to a left ankle sprain.

Ball was initially listed as questionable to play, an encouraging sign after he suffered what first appeared to be a serious ankle injury late in Wednesday night's win over the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Ball landed on one of Thunder center Isaiah Hartenstein's feet and had to be helped off the court after going down in pain.

Acquired in an offseason trade with the Charlotte Hornets, Ball has been a driving force in the Timberwolves' early-season success. Minnesota enters Friday's game at 14-5 and tied for third in the Western Conference despite the absence of All-Star shooting guard Anthony Edwards.

There isn't a firm timetable for Edwards' return, but he is expected to miss several more weeks.

A win over the Grizzlies would clinch West Group B for the Timberwolves and advance them into the quarterfinals of the NBA Cup.

Ball, 25, is averaging 17.3 points and 5.7 assists for Minnesota this season.

articles.headline: NFL Week 12 arrivals: Cameron Heyward leads arrivals ahead of Steelers-Broncos
articles.description: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
articles.body:
The Thanksgiving menu includes an extra helping of NFL style, with Week 12 arrivals getting started before the turkey hits the table.

The Green Bay Packers visited the Los Angeles Rams on a warm Wednesday in Inglewood, California.

Thursday brings the Chicago Bears and Detroit Lions together in Detroit, and morning temperatures in the 40s could lead to giving statement coats their moment. The Philadelphia Eagles visit the Dallas Cowboys in Arlington, Texas, where a sunny afternoon in the 50s calls for sweater weather.

The Kansas City Chiefs face the Buffalo Bills on Thursday night in Orchard Park, New York, to close out the tripleheader with temperatures in the 30s and rain in the forecast. Friday's meeting between the Denver Broncos and Pittsburgh Steelers in Pittsburgh brings another opportunity for layers, with temperatures around the low 40s and possible showers.

Sunday offers a little of everything: jacket weather around the Great Lakes, warmer conditions in South Florida and potential rain in the Bay Area. Whether players are bundling up or keeping things breezy, there's plenty of room to serve a look.

Here are the standout arrivals from Week 12.

Black Friday fashion

The Steelers and Broncos brought a variety of fits to the tunnels of Acrisure Stadium for their Friday afternoon showdown, with the highlight likely being Cameron Heyward breaking out a sleek -- but still cozy -- turtleneck and chain look.

Thanksgiving threads

Chris Jones brought the style to Buffalo through the inclement weather and all. The Kansas City Chiefs defensive tackle wore a cream double-breasted suit with a black turtleneck.

CeeDee Lamb donned a long black double-breasted overcoat, charcoal trousers and chunky lace-up boots. The Dallas Cowboys wide receiver accessorized with a leather tote and silver jewelry.  Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons embraced fall fashion in a camel-colored coat with plush shearling-style lapels, layered over a plum plaid suit and matching turtleneck. 

Wednesday's looks

Aaron Donald kept it sleek in a black zip-up jacket and matching pants, accessorizing with gold-tinted shades and a checkered designer pouch. His blue, white and yellow sneakers added a pop of Rams colors to the look.

articles.headline: Why Walker Kessler is the X factor for Luka Doncic and the Lakers this season
articles.description: Doncic's first request when he became a Laker? Get an 'A-list' big man. It took a year, but Kessler is that man in Los Angeles.
articles.body:
EVEN INSIDE a busy hotel lobby, one with 30-foot ceilings, a gilded life-sized horse statue, a jungle-gym-looking apparatus covering the bar area and an oversized, magenta, metallic art installation at the front entrance, Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler stands out.

It's late in the evening on Nov. 7.

Dressed in a gray sweatsuit and a black trucker-style baseball cap on an off night in Birmingham, Michigan, Daxton Hotel patrons turn as the 7-foot-2 Kessler walks from the elevator banks to a seat at a four-top table as L.A.'s new man in the middle.

He's used to the attention by now.

"It's the way I'm supposed to be," Kessler told ESPN about his height, which puts him as one of the top 10 tallest players in the NBA. "It's weird for me if my feet didn't hang over the bed -- that would feel uncomfortable with me."

He has looked mighty comfortable right from the start this season, scoring 26 points on 12-for-12 shooting (including 10 dunks), with nine rebounds and two blocks in his Lakers debut in an opening-night rout over Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors.

After the game, he joined the "Inside the NBA" crew and received a stamp of approval from a legendary Lakers center.

"The way you played tonight, you played like the best big man in the league," Shaquille O'Neal told Kessler, who became the first Lakers player since Wilt Chamberlain in 1969 to have that many makes without a miss. "Welcome to the big man alliance."

Just before the segment finished, O'Neal chimed in again.

"I got a new nickname for you," he said. "Your new nickname is, 'Milk Chamberlain.' I love you, Milk."

Though Kessler appreciated O'Neal's compliment, he did push back just a little.

"The Milk Chamberlain is ... I don't think I'm anywhere [close to him] ... I'm not Wilt Chamberlain. But that's clever. It's a funny nickname."

Kessler will, of course, not be expected to match Chamberlain's gaudy production (although Kessler's 66.9% shooting percentage so far in Los Angeles is better than Chamberlain fared in four of his five L.A. seasons).

But after Luka Doncic personally asked for him as his preferred pick-and-roll partner, and the Lakers gave up a bevy of assets to acquire him from the Utah Jazz this summer, he will be expected to play Chamberlain to Doncic's Jerry West and win a championship for the Lakers.

Because after the significant haul the Lakers spent to bring him to L.A., the success of the dawning Doncic era will depend on it.

SLUMPED ON A couch in his Manhattan Beach home, with a fire warming the crisp fall air seeping into the living room and past the open sliding glass door window to his back deck, Doncic takes ownership of the transformative roster move.

"I told them after the season I wanted Walker," Doncic told ESPN of an offseason conversation he had with Rob Pelinka, Lakers president of basketball operations and general manager, and the front office.
